metadata.name: Civic nationalism
metadata.description: The contemporary Scottish SNP variant of civic nationalism: residence-based national belonging, democratic self-determination, European cooperation and a social-democratic programme. This is not every civic nationalist tradition.
metadata.scope: The SNP’s civic and social-democratic Scottish national project, anchored in its 2026 manifesto and checked against the Scottish Government’s 2026–27 budget and independent research on national identity. Scotland means the proposed self-governing nation in national questions; regions means its local territories except the explicitly applicable secession principle. Government delivery is evidence of this variant, not the definition of all civic nationalism. Manifesto intentions and budget allocations are distinguished from completed delivery; the cited budget is evidence of government spending plans, not proof that every allocation has been spent. Strict revision-2 re-audit: assess only source-supported positions on the exact questions. Unsupported empirical comparisons, modern technology analogies and institutional particulars remain unknown. Absence of doctrine is not a neutral position. This draft must not be used to calculate or publish a complete profile. Scottish independence preferences are not automatically transferred to the power of every sub-Scottish region or municipality.
metadata.phrase: A self-governing Scottish nation open to residents of different origins, combining shared citizenship with social protection and cooperation in Europe.

sources.title: Young SNP members: socio-nationalism, identity and politics

axes.brief: Popular self-determination and accountable parliamentary government define the selected civic variant. Specific recall devices are institutional inferences, not manifesto promises. Re-audit: 2 question-level answers are unresolved and cannot support a complete axis placement.
axes.counterEvidence: The SNP’s referendum mandate claim remains contested constitutionally. A democratic national project does not eliminate constitutional limits or guarantee agreement among all residents. Earlier conditional or hypothetical explanations are not evidence of neutrality unless retained with specific support; withdrawn rows identify the gap.

answers.rationale: The programme seeks electoral mandates and an independence referendum, making renewable popular authority central.
A panel of specialists would replace the equal civic participation underpinning the national project.
Residence-based equal political belonging is inconsistent with intelligence-based voting qualifications.
Parliamentary self-government entails legislation through accountable institutions rather than unilateral executive override.
Democratic self-determination requires opponents to compete under equal rules, including opponents of independence.
Public-service spending commitments require parliamentary scrutiny by representatives outside the executive.
The manifesto’s human-rights incorporation supports judicial checks against unlawful government decisions.
Trade unions are partners in this social-democratic programme, not a privileged replacement electorate.
The leadership’s preferred constitutional outcome does not justify excluding peaceful opposing parties.
